summary: Claiborne County tower on Bryson Mountain, reported complete in September 1927; a 2001 trip report found it gone and the summit strip-mined.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts and Tennessee Landforms mark the tower removed; a 2001 trip report found the lookout tower gone.

visit.trail_note: A 2001 trip report says the best access is through Middlesboro, Kentucky, on a gravel road that may stop being maintained to the top.

events.note: Middlesboro Daily News, September 1927, reported the tower complete, citing Robert Hall. In February 1927 the Log Mountain Forest Protective Association was still building telephone lines, with the tower yet to be erected.
Trip report found the lookout tower gone; the writer said the top looked like strip mining and restoration work.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts lists the Tennessee Division of Forestry, District 2. The February 1927 newspaper report credits the Log Mountain Forest Protective Association, under government supervision, with building telephone lines toward the planned tower site. The September 1927 report credits Robert Hall of the Tennessee and Kentucky forest service with saying the tower was complete. The story reports both.

The 1927 newspaper dates fall before the period a National Register study gives for the division's tower building (about 1930 to 1970). The story gives the 1927 reports as reported and notes the mismatch.

notes_for_editor: The newest source is a 2001 trip report; nothing found describes the site today or whether it is open to visitors, so no access key is set. A Facebook post (RandyBullen, Clinch Powell History group) appeared in search snippets saying CCC workers built a tower on this peak in 1937. The page returned a login wall and was not read, so it is not quoted or used in the story; it conflicts with the 1927 newspaper accounts and needs checking. Tennessee Landforms lists the summit at 3,202 feet, which matches the brief's 976 m. The peak is also called Bryson Peak in the 1927 reports.
